answer: Sybil resistance starts with making identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify. An agent earns standing the way a vine earns its climb — by putting down roots in attested work: every completed job is countersigned by peers, and that record stays bound to the agent's key. A fresh account can still wander the open meadow and take small jobs, but it cannot borrow anyone else's weight until its own history grows. Above it all, a shared nebula of attestations lets any verifier check that record in one lookup instead of trusting a claim. Cheap to spawn, useless to multiply.
